facts.text: I have stomach pain.
It started two weeks ago.

facts.item: stomach pain: constant or comes and goes
facts.text: I don't have the pain all the time. It comes and goes.
At least once every day.

facts.item: stomach pain: change since it started
facts.text: It's getting worse.
When I have the pain, it's a 7 out of 10, and then it can go down to 0.
It's right here, in the upper middle part of my stomach.
It doesn't spread anywhere else.

facts.item: stomach pain: what it feels like
facts.text: It's burning.

facts.item: stomach pain: what makes it better
facts.text: Food, antacids and milk make it better. Usually the pain decreases or stops completely when I eat.

facts.item: stomach pain: what makes it worse
facts.text: Large meals and feeling hungry make it worse. The foods that make it worse are heavy, fatty meals, like pizza.

facts.item: stomach pain: timing in relation to meals
facts.text: It comes back 2 to 3 hours after I eat.
I've never had anything like this before.
Sometimes I feel nauseated when I'm in pain.
I vomited.
Yesterday, for the first time.
It was a yellowish, sour liquid.
There was no blood in it.
I haven't had any diarrhea.
I haven't been constipated.
My weight hasn't changed.
My appetite hasn't changed.
I haven't noticed any change in the color of my stools.
I have arthritis in both knees. I take ibuprofen for it.
I had a urinary tract infection 1 year ago. It was treated with amoxicillin.
I had two C-sections.
I take Maalox.
I take ibuprofen for the arthritis in my knees.
Two pills, two to three times a day.
I'm not allergic to any medications.
My father died at 55 of pancreatic cancer.
My mother is alive and healthy.
I don't drink alcohol.
I've never used any illegal substances.
I don't smoke or use any other tobacco products.
I'm sexually active with my husband.
I'm a housewife.
I'm married.

source_issues: Gold diagnosis #3 (Gastritis) is garbled: an empty 'History Finding(s):' header is followed by 'Physical &am Finding(s):' and four mixed bullets. Bullets were assigned by meaning: NSAID use, pain associated with food, and nausea/vomiting to history; epigastric tenderness to exam.
Gold #1 history cites 'four children'; this appears only in the raw patient description ('married with four children'), not in the Q/A or the note (note PSH: 2 C-sections).
The raw 'Sample Closure' is unrelated text (a survey about job interviews), and the closure checklist mentions a rectal exam; neither was used.
p024 asks about the rest of the immediate family, but the answer covers only the parents.
notes: Temporality: facts describing the episodic pattern of the current pain (comes and goes, daily frequency, per-episode severity, return 2-3 hours after eating, nausea during pain) are 'recurrent'; onset, progression, location, quality, radiation, and relieving and aggravating factors are 'current'. Vomiting yesterday (a single event) is 'historical'.

p009 (food relieves) and p012 (eating decreases or stops the pain) are merged into the relieving child f010; p010 'large meals' and p011 'heavy, fatty meals, like pizza' are merged into the aggravating child f011 to avoid paraphrase duplicates.
p017 'Have your bowel movements altered?' 'No' (topic Diarrhea/Constipation) is split into no diarrhea (f019) and no constipation (f020), as in the note HPI.
Stage directions '(points to the epigastrium)', '(laughs)' and '(... if asked)' moved to extras.acting_notes; the ibuprofen dose itself is kept as the child f029.
The patient description 'married with four children' exists only in raw_opening; kept in extras.acting_notes.
The additional-diagnosis bullet 'Other etiologies' lists five diagnoses; split into one record each.

Conversion: v1's separate relieving facts (food, antacids, milk) and aggravating facts (large/fatty meals, hunger) become one relieving and one aggravating child each, with complete value lists, following the reference conversion (medqa-cs-001 f025).
Conversion: the pointing gesture in p006 is given in words for the text-only patient ('in the upper middle part of my stomach'), without the clinical term 'epigastrium'.

Conversion: vomiting (p014) is split into the symptom (f015) and its onset child (f016, 'yesterday, for the first time'); the vomit description (p015) and the absence of blood (p016) are appearance children.
Conversion: the ibuprofen dose, given in the script only 'if asked', is a quantity child (f029) of the ibuprofen fact.

Conversion: the note's 'VS: Within normal limits' (e002) agrees with the doorway values and is cited on each doorway vital record. The SP-simulated right-upper-abdominal pain worse on inspiration is part of the abdominal examination (x009) and of the Murphy sign record (x010); the simulated epigastric tenderness matches the note's abdominal exam.
Harmonisation pass: scale [0, 10] added to f006.

Fixes: f008 answer word removed; f013 answer word removed; f015 answer word removed; f021 answer word removed; f022 answer word removed; f023 answer word removed; f015 time -> resolved; f016 time -> resolved; f017 time -> resolved; f018 time -> resolved; f038 new fact 'marital status' from f036.
